# dsh-open-in-codebuddy
English | 中文
Adds a **CodeBuddy** button to the DSH Session header: one click opens the current Session's workspa
ce folder in CodeBuddy.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Or from npm (prebuilt, no build approval needed):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The package declares `dsh.bundle`, so DSH adopts it as a profile bundle layer on install — no hand-e
diting of `cordis.patch.yml` or `package.json`.
## What you get
A CodeBuddy button appears in the Session header, directly beside DSH's own "Open In..." control and
sharing its geometry:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Clicking it opens CodeBuddy on the current Session's workspace folder. While launching, the button s
hows a busy state; on failure an error notice appears beside it and clears after six seconds. When C
odeBuddy is not detected, the button is not rendered at all.
## Platform support
| Platform | How it launches |
| macOS | CodeBuddy's own `Contents/Resources/app/bin/code -n <dir>`, which opens the folder as a wo

rkspace in a new window; falls back to `open -a` when that CLI is absent |
| Windows / Linux | `code
buddy` / `cbc` / `codebuddy-code` from `PATH`, run with the folder as the working directory |
On macOS the bundle id must be `com.tencent.codebuddycn`, so a renamed install still works while an
unrelated application at the same path is not launched.
### Non-standard install location
`/Applications` and `~/Applications` are searched for `CodeBuddy CN.app` and `CodeBuddy.app`. If you
rs lives elsewhere, set the variable and restart DSH:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## How it works
- **Host half** (`index.js`) detects and launches CodeBuddy behind two routes: `GET /open-in-codebud
dy/status` and `POST /open-in-codebuddy/open`. Both sit behind DSH's connection trust fence (`ctx.co
nnection.requestRejection`), so unauthenticated and cross-origin callers are rejected before any det
ection or launch runs. Request bodies are capped at 64 KiB, must be `application/json`, and the path
must be an existing absolute directory. Launches never go through a shell: arguments are passed as

argv, detached, with no stdio pipes.
- **Client half** (`client.js`) registers under its own cell id
`open-in-codebuddy` in `conversation.session.header.utilities`, so it sits beside DSH's native cont
rol without touching it.
DSH's shipped application catalogue (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-open-in-app`) is a compile-time table wi
th no configuration seam, so a third party cannot append CodeBuddy to that native dropdown. In the s
lot system, a duplicate cell id at the same priority throws, and only a lower priority shadows the n
ative control — which means taking over its UI wholesale. This plugin uses its own cell id instead:
it works on install, reverts on uninstall, and leaves the native control untouched.
## Permissions
The Host half runs with the DSH process's own permissions: it reads application install locations an
d spawns one local process. It makes no network requests, reads no workspace files, and touches no c
e local process. It makes no network requests, reads no workspace files, and touches no credentials.
